_note: Surface-scoped arm for registry_list_workflows, 2026-08-24. Written after the 'it is a duplicate of workflow_list' reason was retracted: the twin declares no arguments and cannot filter by surface.

scenarios.prompt: What workflows are available on the studio surface?
scenarios.prompt_source:
meta.synonyms['what workflows'] VERBATIM AND CONTIGUOUS, plus the one thing this tool can do that its always-on twin cannot: filter by SURFACE.

🔴 THIS IS NOT AN EASIER PROMPT, IT IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION — and the twin gets it WRONG. workflow_list declares properties:{} and cannot narrow; registry_list_workflows takes surface: book|editor|studio. Measured by calling it: 12 / book 12 / editor 11 / STUDIO 6. So answering this with the twin means reporting 12 where 6 is the truth.

Verified against the deployed matcher before this scenario was written: this wording makes registry_list_workflows answerable and it is the ONLY tool in that set.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM knowledge_projects WHERE project_id='{project_id}'
seed_assert.why: The fixture exists. Probed directly: the registry returns curated System workflows with slug + title + description — 'autonomous-drafting' among them — so the list is non-empty and its titles are checkable.

answer_expect.why: The registry returns several System workflows to every account. Reporting none would be a false absence.

scenarios.falsifier:
REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply reports no workflows, OR it describes a workflow's STEPS — the L1 listing returns slug + title + description and explicitly NOT the step list, so an account of what a workflow does step by step in this turn came from the model, not the tool. That is the same L1/L2 boundary registry_get_workflow exists to cross.

ADDED FOR THIS ARM: REFUTED IF the reply reports ALL TWELVE workflows for a question that named the STUDIO surface — the studio has 6 — or if it answers from workflow_list, which cannot filter and would therefore be reporting a number it had no way to narrow. A confident wrong count is worse here than a refusal.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — System defaults are always visible, so an empty registry is not reachable and must not be claimed.
ship_audit.surface_filter: OWED — the filter is the whole reason this arm exists: book|editor|studio must each return their own set, and an invalid surface must be refused rather than silently ignored (ignoring it would return 12 and read as success).

scenarios._control_note:
SURFACE-SCOPED ARM. It does NOT replace registry-list-workflows and does not retire its finding: asked 'What workflows are available to me?', the model answered with workflow_list on 5 of 5 and the answer was TRUE and COMPLETE. That is correct behaviour against an always-on consumer-local twin, and it stays on file.

What that arm could not do is reach this tool, because for the UNFILTERED question the twin is a complete answer. This arm asks the question the twin cannot answer.
